40 Very overrated film. Never understood the hype around that film especially its plot twist. Its plot twist isn’t as good as people say it is for various reasons I’m gonna point out. ⚠️SPOILERS below if you haven’t seen the film⚠️ Firstly, Verbal Kint, a crippled man, knew way too much about everything and everyone. Obviously since he was in that crew but also on everything not relating his crew. The thing that throws me off the most is how good of a storyteller he is and for someone whose partners and friends just died, he’s way too calm not showing his sadness and anger. At first, you can immediately tell he’s different from the others. All of their arrests are shown on screen except Kint before they’re brought in as suspects. Then another thing that is weird is when Fenster, Hockney, Keaton and McManus all get interrogated by the cops in the interrogation room except Verbal Kint again. Even in that prison cell scene, the camera’s focused on these four individuals but then out of the blue comes Verbal Kint who is unknown and excluded for them. All of that in the span of 15minutes can already give you a strong feeling that Kint can be Keyser Soze when you’re deeper into the film. The problem with Verbal Kint is that one moment he’s clumsy, timid and the other moment he’s a good storyteller as if he knows everything about everyone and he’s too curious. When Kobayashi comes in with the briefcase and they find out Keyser Soze’s got info on all of them, they’re all preoccupied, panicking but Verbal Kint himself isn’t really panicking. Instead he’s asking himself who’s Keyser Soze. To Kujan, he was on about how ruthless and powerful Keyser Soze was but he didn’t know who Keyser Soze was prior to that so how did he know all this about Keyser Soze? Halfway through the film, you already know who Keyser Soze is. It’s obviously written on the wall. Small details are always important to remember and that’s why it’s not a good film. You don’t even have to be an expert or whatever to know that Verbal Kint is Keyser Soze. The Usual Suspects is predictable and has multiple flaws that are noticeable based on Verbal Kint’s behavior, that ruthless behavior in the parking lot. There’s missing key plot points that are essential to the story. They try to hide all those flaws but they’re very noticeable. I’ve seen this film twice and in those two times, I’ve seen the flaws that are noticeable. Just base yourself off the psychological aspect of Verbal Kint, his curiosity and his questioning on who Keyser Soze is and suddenly he knows him like a book without knowing him. That’s how you’ll know it’s him. 15 minutes in, you know it’s him, the way he is, how he acts, his voice-over narration, it’s painfully obvious and clear. A 6th grader would have it all figured out. I mean who else could it be ? It’s far from an impressive plot twist and film. And how come Sergeant Rabin never realized Verbal Kint was full of shit and he made this up due to the details on the board of his own office ? It’s his office. As a sergeant, you’re supposed to know what cases you’re working on even if files are piling up on your desk. It doesn’t matter. Even a small detail from your cases that is mentioned by Keyser Soze, you can immediately tell he’s full of lies and has been pretending ever since. The film would’ve ended halfway through immediately that way. It’s not even that complex. The performances aren’t impressive. Gabriel Byrne’s Irish accent can be heard and noticed at times. The storytelling itself gives away more than it should.

Noirvember #3 - The Usual Suspects " The film's coup de grace is as elegant as it is unexpected. The whole movie plays back in your mind in perfect clarity—and turns out to be a completely different movie to the one you've been watching (rather better, in fact). " - Quentin Curtis (The Independent) Incredibly on point! My words exact! Holy shit! I’d hate to spoil anything from The Usual Suspects . This is a movie that benefits not knowing anything and going in blind. A deconstruction of the Neo-noir movies of the 80's and 90's and dare I say an incredibly tightly written subversion at that! Like the movie was tethering at a solid 7 or 8 for most of the runtime, but that final scene man. Immediately skyrocketed the score up another point. You can’t execute a mindfuck as crazy and unexpected as the one in The Usual Suspects and that’s all I’ll say regarding the narrative. Immensely deserving of its Best Original Screenplay Oscar win. The whole film is well made from every technical standpoint given its rather small $6 million budget. The way the film is shot and framed doesn’t make it look a day old. You could’ve told me this movie came out this year and I would’ve believed you. The only difference is that it doesn’t have that shitty gray color hue that every modern movies needs to have nowadays. I also liked how ominous the score was, particularly during the opening credits. Setting the tone and mystery for the film. Surprised the composer also edited the film too. All of the performances were a slam dunk but the clear highlight has to be Kevin Spacey. Now I know he’s, you know, but you have to remember why he was considered one of the best actors of his time. Separating Spacey the person to Spacey the character he’s playing. Here, he’s so deceiving and manipulative while playing innocent and humble. He’s so layered and complex and is the driving force of this bonkers narrative that has you guessing at every turn. Spacey, even if you hate to admit it, was deserving of his Best Supporting Actor win through the nuance and depth he plays here. The catalyst that makes the mystery so fucking good!!!! While everyone else is binge watching Bryan Singer’s X-Men films to get ready for Avengers Doomsday . Here I am watching one of Singer's most critically acclaimed films and really the only one he’s deserves to be remembered by because like Kevin Spacey, Bryan Singer is also a piece of shit in real life. I don’t even think Singer is all that good of a director. The screenplay by Christopher McQuarrie is what carries the film here. Making The Usual Suspects an admittedly slow and confusing burner at first, but once the mystery unfolds. You’re left absolutely speechless. Biggest mindfuck I’ve experienced in a movie in recent memory.
